book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Engineer traps nasty brute in barrel

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so the word beside it is to be mangled into a new order
to trap something is to hold it inside, so the first piece goes round the second

blocks.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame
the five letters of brute, scrambled

explanation.surface: A thug is shut inside a barrel by an engineer, like a scene from a gangster film.
explanation.walkthrough: Engineer looks like the definition at the front of the clue, but it is a famous name; the definition is barrel at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-butt is a large barrel set under a downpipe to collect rainwater, so it is a kind of barrel.

clue.text: ADRSCNOUAWN One horseman's drier

blocks.note: scanning debris printed before the clue, not part of it
one is the article a
a horseman is a rider; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A horse rider's drier, as though the jockey owned a tumble dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of horseman's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means dry, so its comparative form, more arid, is a synonym for drier.

clue.text: Cottage's last flower for festival

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the possessive word is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of cottage
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A country cottage grows its final bloom in time for a village festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection, held each spring.

clue.text: Drinker shut in quite without air

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following word's letters are taken out of the word before

blocks.note: to bar someone in is to shut them in
fairly means quite, as in fairly good
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A drinker locked into a stuffy room with no fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone sealed in without ventilation; in fact the air comes out of a word meaning quite, not out of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A barfly is a person who spends a lot of time drinking in bars, so a habitual drinker.

clue.text: Suffer in bed?

blocks.note: surface reading: to be ill and confined to bed
setter's reading: to put up with an insult meekly, which in bed one would literally be doing horizontally

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for accepting ill treatment without protest is read literally: someone in bed is horizontal while they endure it.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept an insult or setback passively without fighting back is the idiom's meaning, matching suffer.

clue.text: Supernatural, power blasted smart soldier

indicators.note: something blasted has been blown apart, so the following word's letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: mana is a Polynesian word for supernatural power
the letters of smart, scrambled

explanation.surface: A smart soldier is hit by some supernatural force, as in a fantasy battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits supernatural from power, but the two words together give one piece; smart soldier also wants to read as a unit, though smart is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-at-arms is an armed fighting man, especially a mounted medieval soldier.

clue.text: Shameless grubby cafe cooked bread outside

indicators.note: grubby means messed up and dirty, so the word after it is to be jumbled
cooked suggests something altered or fiddled, so the word after it is rearranged
outside says the second piece wraps around the first

blocks.note: the letters of bread, rearranged
the letters of cafe, rearranged

explanation.surface: A greasy-spoon cafe brazenly serving baked goods, a picture of a shameless eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: Both anagram indicators sit before their words: grubby works on cafe and cooked works on bread, and the bread anagram then goes round the cafe one.
explanation.definitionFit: Barefaced means openly brazen without any attempt at disguise, as in a barefaced lie, so it means shameless.

clue.text: What esnes do to be rational

blocks.note: surface reading: an odd nonsense word, apparently describing some creature's behaviour
setter's reading: esnes is a familiar word written backwards, so turned the right way round these letters spell out sense

explanation.walkthrough: Esnes is no word at all until it is read from the end, when it becomes a real one: so esnes, put the right way round, literally form sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sense is to be logical and understandable, which is what being rational means.

clue.text: Fruit's not entirely crazy

indicators.note: not entirely means falling a little short, so the word's final letter is dropped

blocks.note: bananas is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit described as slightly mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a long yellow-skinned tropical fruit, an obvious example of fruit.

clue.text: Couple's lost their first cycle in bombing raid

indicators.note: losing their first means the opening letter is dropped from the word for the couple

blocks.note: a couple is a pair; with the 's it is pair's
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: A couple lose their first bicycle in an air raid, a wartime hard-luck tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Their refers back to the couple only, so the cycle keeps all its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-strike is an attack made by aircraft, so a bombing raid is exactly one.

clue.text: Rush with most excellent inflorescence

blocks.note: to rush is to race
ME is the abbreviation of Most Excellent, an honorific title

explanation.surface: Hurrying past the finest blossom in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Most Excellent is a formal style of address, abbreviated ME, used in some orders and titles.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower cluster with stalked flowers along a central stem, a botanical type of inflorescence.

clue.text: Small enclosure on rough Alpine land surface that's denuded

indicators.note: rough means crude or unpolished, so the following word's letters come out in a disordered state

blocks.note: a pen is a small enclosure for animals
the letters of alpine, rearranged

explanation.surface: A little sheepfold sits on rugged mountain ground stripped bare.
explanation.walkthrough: On is placement in an across clue: the pen comes first, sitting on the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A peneplain is a geology term for a nearly flat land surface produced by long erosion, so it has been worn bare.

clue.text: Is able to copy accompaniment to cocktails

blocks.note: if one is able to, one can
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: Someone who can imitate whatever accompanies the drinks at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A canape is a small savoury snack on bread or pastry, typically served with drinks at a cocktail party.

clue.text: She grooms pinto at last restless after running

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the horse word
running suggests movement out of place, so the letters of the word before are set loose and reordered
after says the jumbled piece follows the single letter rather than coming before it

blocks.note: the final letter of pinto
the letters of restless, rearranged

explanation.surface: A stablegirl finally settles a restless piebald horse after it has been out running.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinto is a piebald horse, which makes the stable picture seamless.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostleress is a female ostler, a woman who looks after horses at an inn, so she grooms them.

clue.text: Refit gear to work in space under chimney

definitions.note: the grate is what stands in that space, rather than the space itself

indicators.note: putting letters to work sets them moving into a different, functional arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of refit and gear together, rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer refitting equipment so it can operate in a cramped space below a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: Refit looks like the instruction, but it is part of the fodder; in links the result to where it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-grate is the iron frame holding the fuel in a hearth, which sits in the fireplace beneath the chimney.

clue.text: Prod about inside residue

indicators.note: inside says the small piece is placed within the larger word

blocks.note: a prod can be a reminder, a nudge to the memory
A is a dictionary abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Poking around in some leftover sediment.
explanation.walkthrough: About usually signals a container or a reversal, but here it is a letter that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A remainder is what is left over after the rest is removed, which is what residue means.

clue.text: In the manner of a side petal

blocks.note: first meaning: the French phrase a la, as in a la carte
second meaning: in botany, either of the two lateral petals of a pea flower

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one botanical description; it is two meanings split before a.
explanation.definitionFit: A la is borrowed French for in the style of, and ala is the Latin-derived botanical name for a wing petal.

clue.text: Redcap follows a unit

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the police piece goes behind the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
redcap is slang for a British military policeman, an MP

explanation.surface: A military policeman tails a squad of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcaps are so called from the red tops of their caps.
explanation.definitionFit: The amp, short for ampere, is the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Worried goddess

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of eat in the sense of trouble, as in what's eating you
second meaning: the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads as an anxious deity; each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that ate at you worried you, and Ate is the Greek goddess who led people into rash acts.

clue.text: What the ball that bowls me does

definitions.text: What the ball that bowls me does

blocks.note: surface reading: a cricketer describing the delivery that gets them out
setter's reading: a cricketer's timbers are the wooden stumps, which the ball smashes, so the stock pirate oath becomes literal

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the stumps and bails are called the timbers, and being bowled means the ball has hit them; shiver is an old word for shatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball that bowls a batsman scatters their stumps, literally shattering their timbers, the phrase pirates use as an oath.

clue.text: Power that's a welcome luxury

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A sense of power, enjoyed as a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a rich baked treat, the kind of indulgence that comes as a welcome extra.

clue.text: Room to manoeuvre by river path

blocks.note: the Lee is a river in London and in Ireland
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Room to turn a boat around near a riverside towpath.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is the freedom of action or margin available, an idiomatic word for room to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Victim — pedestrian with packed hamper

indicators.note: packed means stowed inside, so the letters sit within the words before

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A road accident victim, a pedestrian, carrying a loaded basket.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamper looks like a picnic basket in the surface; it is the verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to obstruct or slow progress, so it is a synonym for the verb hamper.

clue.text: Beater finds small child below top of spinney by river

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
in a down entry, below means the child piece is written under the single letter

blocks.note: the first letter of spinney
a mite is a small child
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A beater on a shoot finds a toddler at the edge of a copse beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Beater suggests the person who drives game birds on a shoot, matching the spinney (a small wood); here it just means one who strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiter is one who smites, that is strikes hard, so a beater in the literal sense.

clue.text: Gloomy month with girl

blocks.note: mo. is the standard abbreviation for month
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl feeling down for a whole month.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose describes a sullen, sour, gloomy temperament.

clue.text: Greek king, Turkish chief and Ethiopian king

blocks.note: an aga is an Ottoman Turkish commander or chief
Memnon was the king of the Ethiopians in Greek myth, killed by Achilles at Troy

explanation.surface: A list of three rulers from Greece, Turkey and Ethiopia, like a summit roll-call.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface lists three monarchs; the first is the definition and the other two build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greek army against Troy.

clue.text: Full of enthusiasm for breeding without energy

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for the following word is removed

blocks.note: rearing animals is breeding them
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Keen on stockbreeding but lacking the stamina for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means eager and keen to start, so bursting with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Chief magistrate to follow ruthless self-interest

definitions.note: the phrase is usually an adjective, here used as a noun for cut-throat rivalry

blocks.note: the Doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
to and at both mark direction or position, as in at the door
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A head magistrate who pursues his own interests without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doge of Venice is the classic crossword chief magistrate; the pieces ignore the answer's word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog eat dog describes a fiercely competitive world where everyone looks after themselves at others' expense.

clue.text: Senate dressed in glossy fabric

indicators.note: something dressed has been prepared or arranged, so the word's letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of senate, rearranged

explanation.surface: Roman senators attired in shiny cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sateen is a cotton cloth woven to have a glossy, satin-like surface.

clue.text: Ignorant one deserved pound first

indicators.note: first says the money piece is placed ahead of the word meaning deserved

blocks.note: 'un is dialect for one, as in a good 'un
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound sterling
what you have earned you have deserved

explanation.surface: An uneducated person thinks they merited a pound up front.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlearned means not educated or lacking knowledge, which is what ignorant describes.
